title: implement an authenticated storage operation with the supported SDK
input: The developer selects the actual Azure SDK package and the application's required storage operation.
action: The selected SDK serializes supported API requests, handles configured authentication and exposes service responses to application code. It is a client library; the remote Azure service performs the storage operation.
output: The application uses its managed identity to write or read the approved blob and handles the returned status.
check: Test package compatibility, least-privilege identity, retry ambiguity and failures against the actual service endpoint.

service: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
title: run a licensed relational application on a managed VM host
input: The database owner prepares supported SQL Server software, storage layout and restricted application accounts.
action: SQL Server on the VM executes SQL and stores relational data on its configured volumes. Azure supplies the VM infrastructure and selected integrations; the owner defines database maintenance, availability and backup responsibilities.
output: The backend commits authorized transactions and returns results using its restricted SQL login or identity integration.
check: Test transaction behavior, host recovery, database-consistent restore, licensing and the chosen high-availability configuration.

title: inspect and transfer an authorized storage dataset
input: The operator selects the correct tenant, storage account and approved file-transfer scope.
action: Storage Explorer provides a client interface for supported Azure storage operations under the selected identity. The remote storage service persists the data; client browsing does not bypass account permissions.
output: The operator uploads or retrieves the approved files and records the transfer result.
check: Check target account, object paths, checksums and access denial before treating the transfer as complete.

title: build and debug a reviewed application revision
input: The developer checks out the approved project and configures its supported toolchain.
action: Visual Studio supplies the IDE, compiler integration and debugging tools for the project. Application code and selected build tools create the artifact; the IDE does not automatically grant deployment permissions.
output: The developer verifies the change locally and submits the reviewed revision to the release pipeline.
check: Test build reproducibility, debug-secret handling and acceptance behavior before promoting the artifact.

title: develop a containerized API with reviewed editor extensions
input: The developer opens the approved repository and selects trusted project extensions.
action: VS Code provides the editor and configured extension or task integrations. Build tasks execute the chosen tools and remote APIs use their own credentials; an editor workspace is not an application hosting service.
output: The developer runs the API's tests and submits accepted code through the repository workflow.
check: Check extension trust, workspace settings, secret handling and reproducible command-line builds before release.

title: host a corporate application with explicit operating-system maintenance
input: The platform team selects a supported server image and application installation requirements.
action: Windows Server supplies the operating system executing the installed application and its configured services. Domain, firewall, patch and storage settings define the host boundary; the application performs business processing.
output: Corporate users reach the approved application endpoint and protected data dependencies.
check: Test host hardening, patch compatibility, identity access and application-consistent restoration before rollout.

title: run a locked-down industrial terminal application
input: The device team selects supported Windows IoT hardware, edition and kiosk application settings.
action: Windows for IoT supplies the selected device operating system and supported lockdown capabilities. The terminal application handles operator input and exchanges authorized messages with the enterprise backend.
output: The backend validates terminal requests and returns the permitted manufacturing or retail operation result.
check: Test kiosk escape restrictions, software updates, device authentication and offline recovery on the actual terminal.
